newsitem.title: USA: Xylan says comfortable with Q4 estimates.
newsitem.headline: Xylan says comfortable with Q4 estimates.

text.p: Xylan Corp said it is comfortable with what it considers to be Wall Street's consensus estimates for the fourth quarter, and said it expects some minimal, one month slippage in two product areas.

"We said we were comfortable with what we perceive as being the sell-side consensus of $41 to $42 million in the December quarter and 11 cents to 12 cents earnings per share in the December quarter," said Douglas Hill, Xylan's vice president for corporate communications.

Xylan's stock was halted, news pending, at midafternoon and never resumed trade on Nasdaq. The last trade was at 31, down five, in the Nasdaq market, although the share was reported to have been selling as high as 34-3/4 in after-hours trade.
Earlier, the share had traded as low as 29-3/4, its lowest trading level since its public debut in March at $26.

Xylan said it would issue a news release later in the day, but did not consider itself to have any material developments to report, noting it had been subject to rumors and speculation regarding upcoming product delivery cycles.

"There was a great deal of rumor that has been swirling around, people have been thinking that there's enormous product delays and, in fact, what we've been talking about is a one-month delay," Hill said.
He said this magnitude of delay would impact two products.

Shipment of its OmniCell asychronous tranfer mode ATM cell switching products will slip to January from December, he said, while new ethernet and fast-ethernet ASIC-based technology will slip into the April time frame from March.
"We don't see a one-month slip to be a material issue," said Hill, adding Xylan has discussed the slippage previously.

Xylan has been one of the year's high-flying initial public offerings, as shares of high-speed computer network switch maker more than doubled on their first day of trade and have soared has high as 76 in the nine months since its debut.
Xylan executives made a presentation on Wednesday to a DMG Technology conference in Phoenix, Arizona, where they repeated their comfort level with current estimates, the company said.

In a research note issued before Thursday's market open, however, DMG Technology analyst Noel Lindsay noted the revenue range referred to by Xylan as the consensus for the fourth quarter was below his own estimate of around $43 million.

"Noel Lindsay, the sell-side analyst at DMG, has had an above consensus estimate of $43.3 or $43.4 million and we're saying that we are not willing to say at this point that we're comfortable at with that number," Hill said.
Hill also noted there has been a "very substantial" short position in the stock."I believe there was a significant amount of rumor and innuendo today in the market," he said.
"My opinion is what we've had here is a tempest in a teapot," he said. "It would not appear that there is a significant change in the information that's publicly available about the company."
First Call's mean estimate from five analysts was for earnings in the fourth quarter of 11 cents a share.

"Looking ahead, we don't see any reason why people should have a problem with the March consensus and we're not feeling rather strongly about the company's performance post-March. We think there's perhaps more upside to the estimates in the June and later quarters than we had been seeing previously."
March estimates were not immediately available. The full year 1997 estimate is for earnings of 74 cents a share.
